VS1 – Cruise configuration stall at gross weight, power off
VX – Best Angle of Climb Speed
VY – Best Rate of Climb Speed
Gliding distance is approximately 1.7 nautical miles (2 statute miles) for each 1000 feet of altitude above terrain.

items.detail: Increase Speed to Blow Out Fire

sections.title: Engine Fire During Start On Ground

items.text: If fire is in engine compartment:
All Other Switch except Ignition Switch
If fire appears out and electrical power necessary to continue flight:

items.detail: One at a time, with delay to locate fault

items.text: After discharging an extinguisher within a closed cabin, ventilate the cabin.

Continuous engine operation with carburetor heat on is not recommended due to the decrease in engine efficiency. If severe icing conditions require extended use of carburetor heat the engine mixture should be leaned during use of carburetor heat.

items.detail: (do not exceed red line) and periodically change RPM to minimize ice buildup on propeller blades.

items.text: Turn back or change altitude to obtain outside air conditions that are less likely to cause icing.
If icing continues plan a landing at the nearest airport. Under extremely rapid icing conditions select a suitable emergency landing site.
With an ice accumulation on or near the wing leading edges a higher stalling speed may be expected. Plan all maneuvers accordingly.
Airspeed – If possible increase airspeed and fly at a higher than normal cruise speed until a landing is begun.
Approach for landing at a higher airspeed than normal depending on amount of ice accumulation.

sections.title: Landing With a Flat Main Tire

items.detail: Hold airplane off flat tire as long as possible

sections.title: Landing With a Flat Nosewheel Tire

items.detail: Hold nose gear off runway as long as possible
Allow airplane to roll to a stop if possible

items.text: If Field Circuit Breaker is tripped, land as soon as practical.
If Field Circuit Breaker is not tripped, and ammeter continues to show discharge, set alternator side of master switch to OFF and land as soon as practical.
Do not touch pitot tube directly. It can be hot enough to burn skin.
Engine is ready for takeoff when it will take throttle without hesitating or faltering and oil temperature is in green arc.
VY – Best Rate of Climb Speed
VX – Best Angle of Climb Speed
Do not open canopy at speeds in excess of 130 MPH.
While descending avoid continuous operation at engine speeds between 1850 and 2250 RPM.
Lower nose wheel slowly as speed decreases.
Use rudder to maintain directional control down to approx. 20 MPH.
Brakes – Use as required for stopping and directional control
